learning_outcomes.text: Understand and apply the fundamentals of linear algebra to matrix manipulation and solving systems of equations.
Understand and apply differential equation solving techniques in the context of engineering problems.
Understand and apply common numerical methods in solving engineering problems.
Solve optimization and simulation problems similar to those encountered in engineering by selecting and applying appropriate methods.
Acquire agility in calculating and manipulating mathematical expressions.
Identify a mathematical problem, apply the necessary techniques to solve it, and evaluate the results obtained.
Model engineering-related problems using mathematical tools and proceed to solve them.
Understand and rigorously use mathematical language.
Able to reason abstractly, with logical and algorithmic thinking.
Able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Euclidean Affine Geometry and Differential Geometry
teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts related to the subjects and problem-solving sessions; group discussions and sharing.
Personal study, report writing, practical exercises, etc., as independent work by students or student groups.

assessment_methods.method: Written exercises (Block 2, last teaching day of May)

assessment_rules: June final exam: if the student does not reach a grade of 5, they will be re-examined only on the failed block. July extraordinary exam: global value of 100% of the subject.
